sanskrit: tato droṇo mahārāja kekayaṃ vai viśeṣayan prāduścakre raṇe divyaṃ brāhmam astraṃ mahātapāḥ
english: Then, O great king, Droṇa of mighty austerities, singling out the Kekaya prince, brought forth in battle the divine Brahmā weapon.

sanskrit: tad asya rājan kaikeyaḥ pratyavārayad acyutaḥ brāhmeṇaiva mahābāhur āhave samudīritam
english: That weapon, O king, the unshaken Kaikeya of mighty arms warded off in the fray, countering it with the very Brahmā weapon as it was launched.

sanskrit: pratihanya tad astraṃ tu bhāradvājasya saṃyuge vivyādha brāhmaṇaṃ ṣaṣṭyā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Having beaten back that weapon of the son of Bharadvāja in the encounter, he pierced the brāhmaṇa with sixty stone-whetted shafts feathered with gold.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇo dvipadāṃ śreṣṭho nārācena samarpayat sa tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā prāviśad dharaṇītalam
english: Droṇa, foremost among men, answered him with an iron arrow, which, cleaving his armour, sank into the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasarpo yathā mukto valmīkaṃ nṛpasattama tathābhyagān mahīṃ bāṇo bhittvā kaikeyam āhave
english: As a black serpent set loose enters an anthill, O best of kings, so did that arrow, having pierced the Kaikeya in the fight, enter the earth.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja droṇenāstravidā bhṛśam krodhena mahatāviṣṭo vyāvṛtya nayane śubhe
english: Sorely pierced, O great king, by Droṇa the master of weapons, and seized with a mighty wrath, he rolled his fair eyes.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ vivyādha saptatyā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: He pierced Droṇa with seventy stone-whetted shafts feathered with gold, and struck his charioteer with a broad-headed arrow upon the arms and breast.

sanskrit: droṇas tu bahudhā viddho bṛhatkṣatreṇa māriṣa asṛjad viśikhāṃs tīkṣṇān kekayasya rathaṃ prati
english: But Droṇa, pierced in many places by Bṛhatkṣatra, O noble one, let fly sharp arrows toward the Kekaya's chariot.

sanskrit: vyākulīkṛtya taṃ droṇo bṛhatkṣatraṃ mahāratham vyasṛjat sāyakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kekayaṃ prati bhārata
english: Having thrown Bṛhatkṣatra, that great car-warrior, into confusion, Droṇa loosed a keen arrow toward the Kekaya, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddhas tenāśu mahārāja stanāntare rathāt puruṣaśārdūlaḥ saṃbhinnahṛdayo 'patat
english: Deeply pierced by it at once between the breasts, O great king, that tiger among men, his heart cleft asunder, fell from his chariot.

sanskrit: bṛhatkṣatre hate rājan kekayānāṃ mahārathe śaiśupāliḥ susaṃkruddho yantāram idam abravīt
english: When Bṛhatkṣatra, the great car-warrior of the Kekayas, was slain, O king, the son of Śiśupāla, greatly enraged, spoke thus to his driver:

sanskrit: sārathe yāhi yatraiṣa droṇas tiṣṭhati daṃśitaḥ vinighnan kekayān sarvān pāñcālānāṃ ca vāhinīm
english: "Charioteer, drive to where this mailed Droṇa stands, slaughtering all the Kekayas and the host of the Pāñcālas."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sārathī rathināṃ varam droṇāya prāpayām āsa kāmbojair javanair hayaiḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, the charioteer bore that foremost of car-warriors toward Droṇa with swift Kāmboja steeds.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuś ca cedīnām ṛṣabho 'tibaloditaḥ sahasā prāpatad droṇaṃ pataṃga iva pāvakam
english: And Dhṛṣṭaketu, the bull among the Cedis, of surpassing might, fell suddenly upon Droṇa as a moth falls upon the flame.

sanskrit: so 'bhyavidhyat tato droṇaṃ ṣaṣṭyā sāśvarathadhvajam punaś cānyaiḥ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ suptaṃ vyāghraṃ tudann iva
english: He pierced Droṇa, with his horses, car, and standard, with sixty arrows, and again with other keen shafts, as one prodding a sleeping tiger.

sanskrit: tasya droṇo dhanurmadhye kṣurapreṇa śitena ha ciccheda rājño balino yatamānasya saṃyuge
english: Droṇa, with a sharp razor-headed arrow, cut asunder in the middle the bow of that mighty king as he strove in the encounter.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya śaiśupālir mahārathaḥ vivyādha sāyakair droṇaṃ punaḥ suniśitair dṛḍhaiḥ
english: Then the son of Śiśupāla, that great car-warrior, taking up another bow, pierced Droṇa again with sharp and sturdy arrows.

sanskrit: tasya droṇo hayān hatvā sārathiṃ ca mahābalaḥ athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā sāyakānāṃ samārpayat
english: Droṇa of mighty strength, having slain his horses and his charioteer, then assailed him with twenty-five arrows.

sanskrit: viratho vidhanuṣkaś ca cedirājo 'pi saṃyuge gadāṃ cikṣepa saṃkruddho bhāradvājarathaṃ prati
english: Deprived of his car and bereft of his bow, the king of the Cedis too, enraged in the fray, hurled his mace toward the chariot of the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā ghorarūpāṃ bhayāvahām aśmasāramayīṃ gurvīṃ tapanīyavibhūṣitām śarair anekasāhasrair bhāradvājo nyapātayat
english: That mace, rushing down in sudden onset—of terrible form and fearsome, heavy, made of iron and adorned with gold—the son of Bharadvāja brought to the ground with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: sā papāta gadā bhūmau bhāradvājena sāditā raktamālyāmbaradharā tāreva nabhasas talāt
english: That mace, struck down by the son of Bharadvāja, fell to the earth, decked with red garlands and cloth, like a star falling from the floor of heaven.

sanskrit: gadāṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭaketur amarṣaṇaḥ tomaraṃ vyasṛjat tūrṇaṃ śaktiṃ ca kanakojjvalām
english: Seeing his mace struck down, the wrathful Dhṛṣṭaketu swiftly let fly a lance and a gold-gleaming spear.

sanskrit: tomaraṃ tu tribhir bāṇair droṇaś chittvā mahāmṛdhe śaktiṃ ciccheda sahasā kṛtahasto mahābalaḥ
english: But Droṇa, deft of hand and of mighty strength, cleaving the lance with three arrows in that great battle, sundered the spear at once.

sanskrit: tato 'sya viśikhaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vadhārthaṃ vadhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ preṣayām āsa samare bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān
english: Then the glorious son of Bharadvāja, bent on his death, sent against him in battle a sharp arrow to slay him.

sanskrit: sa tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā hṛdayaṃ cāmitaujasaḥ abhyagād dharaṇīṃ bāṇo haṃsaḥ padmasaro yathā
english: That arrow, cleaving the armour and the heart of him of measureless might, entered the earth as a wild goose enters a lotus-pool.

sanskrit: pataṃgaṃ hi grasec cāṣo yathā rājan bubhukṣitaḥ tathā droṇo 'grasac chūro dhṛṣṭaketuṃ mahāmṛdhe
english: As a hungry blue jay, O king, devours a moth, so did the heroic Droṇa devour Dhṛṣṭaketu in that great battle.

sanskrit: nihate cedirāje tu tat khaṇḍaṃ pitryam āviśat amarṣavaśam āpannaḥ putro 'sya paramāstravit
english: When the king of the Cedis was slain, his son, a master of the highest weapons, overcome by wrath, took his stand in his father's portion of the field.

sanskrit: tam api prahasan droṇaḥ śarair ninye yamakṣayam mahāvyāghro mahāraṇye mṛgaśāvaṃ yathā balī
english: Him too Droṇa, smiling, sent with his arrows to the abode of Yama, as a mighty tiger in the great forest carries off a fawn.

sanskrit: teṣu prakṣīyamāṇeṣu pāṇḍaveyeṣu bhārata jarāsaṃdhasuto vīraḥ svayaṃ droṇam upādravat
english: As the warriors of the Pāṇḍava side were being thus destroyed, O descendant of Bharata, the heroic son of Jarāsaṃdha himself rushed against Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa tu droṇaṃ mahārāja chādayan sāyakaiḥ śitaiḥ adṛśyam akarot tūrṇaṃ jalado bhāskaraṃ yathā
english: And he, O great king, veiling Droṇa with sharp arrows, swiftly made him unseen, as a rain-cloud veils the sun.

sanskrit: tasya tal lāghavaṃ dṛṣṭvā droṇaḥ kṣatriyamardanaḥ vyasṛjat sāyakāṃs tūrṇaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Beholding that lightness of hand, Droṇa, the crusher of warriors, swiftly loosed his arrows by the hundred and the thousand.

sanskrit: chādayitvā raṇe droṇo rathasthaṃ rathināṃ varam jārāsaṃdhim atho jaghne miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: Having covered him over in battle, Droṇa then slew the son of Jarāsaṃdha, that foremost of car-warriors standing in his car, before the eyes of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: yo yaḥ sma līyate droṇaṃ taṃ taṃ droṇo 'ntakopamaḥ ādatta sarvabhūtāni prāpte kāle yathāntakaḥ
english: Whoever closed with Droṇa, him Droṇa, like the Ender himself, took away, as the Ender at the appointed hour takes away all living beings.

sanskrit: tato droṇo maheṣvāso nāma viśrāvya saṃyuge śarair anekasāhasraiḥ pāṇḍaveyān vyamohayat
english: Then Droṇa, the mighty archer, proclaiming his name aloud in the battle, bewildered the warriors of the Pāṇḍava side with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: tato droṇāṅkitā bāṇāḥ svarṇapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ narān nāgān hayāṃś caiva nijaghnuḥ sarvato raṇe
english: Then the arrows that bore Droṇa's mark, gold-feathered and stone-whetted, struck down men, elephants, and horses on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā droṇena śakreṇeva mahāsurāḥ samakampanta pāñcālā gāvaḥ śītārditā iva
english: Slaughtered by Droṇa as the great asuras by Śakra, the Pāñcālas trembled like cattle tormented by the cold.

sanskrit: tato niṣṭānako ghoraḥ pāṇḍavānām ajāyata droṇena vadhyamāneṣu sainyeṣu bharatarṣabha
english: Then a terrible wailing arose among the Pāṇḍavas as their troops were being slain by Droṇa, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: mohitāḥ śaravarṣeṇa bhāradvājasya saṃyuge ūrugrāhagṛhītā hi pāñcālānāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Bewildered by the arrow-shower of the son of Bharadvāja in the fight, the great car-warriors of the Pāñcālas were as if seized by a cramp in the thighs.

sanskrit: cedayaś ca mahārāja sṛñjayāḥ somakās tathā abhyadravanta saṃhṛṣṭā bhāradvājaṃ yuyutsayā
english: And the Cedis, O great king, and the Sṛñjayas and the Somakas, eager and exultant, rushed upon the son of Bharadvāja with longing for battle.

sanskrit: hata droṇaṃ hata droṇam iti te droṇam abhyayuḥ yatantaḥ puruṣavyāghrāḥ sarvaśaktyā mahādyutim ninīṣanto raṇe droṇaṃ yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: "Slay Droṇa, slay Droṇa!" crying thus, those tigers among men advanced upon Droṇa, striving with all their might, seeking in battle to send that one of great splendour to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: yatamānāṃs tu tān vīrān bhāradvājaḥ śilīmukhaiḥ yamāya preṣayām āsa cedimukhyān viśeṣataḥ
english: But those striving heroes the son of Bharadvāja sent on to Yama with his shafts, the chiefs of the Cedis above all.

sanskrit: teṣu prakṣīyamāṇeṣu cedimukhyeṣu bhārata pāñcālāḥ samakampanta droṇasāyakapīḍitāḥ
english: As those chiefs of the Cedis were being destroyed, O descendant of Bharata, the Pāñcālas, sorely pressed by Droṇa's arrows, trembled.

sanskrit: prākrośan bhīmasenaṃ te dhṛṣṭadyumnarathaṃ prati dṛṣṭvā droṇasya karmāṇi tathārūpāṇi māriṣa
english: Seeing such deeds of Droṇa, O noble one, they cried out to Bhīmasena and toward the chariot of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇena tapo nūnaṃ caritaṃ duścaraṃ mahat tathā hi yudhi vikrānto dahati kṣatriyarṣabhān
english: "Surely this brāhmaṇa has performed some mighty penance, hard to perform, that he so prevails in battle and consumes the bulls among the warriors."

sanskrit: dharmo yuddhaṃ kṣatriyasya brāhmaṇasya paraṃ tapaḥ tapasvī kṛtavidyaś ca prekṣitenāpi nirdahet
english: "War is the duty of the warrior, but austerity the highest calling of the brāhmaṇa; an ascetic accomplished in learning could burn up a foe with a mere glance."

sanskrit: droṇāstram agnisaṃsparśaṃ praviṣṭāḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ bahavo dustaraṃ ghoraṃ yatrādahyanta bhārata
english: Into Droṇa's weapon, whose touch is like fire, many bulls among the warriors have entered, O descendant of Bharata, and there, beyond crossing and terrible, have been consumed.

sanskrit: yathābalaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yathāsattvaṃ mahādyutiḥ mohayan sarvabhūtāni droṇo hanti balāni naḥ
english: "Each according to his strength, his zeal, his courage—Droṇa of great splendour, confounding all beings, slays our forces."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kṣatradharmā vyavasthitaḥ ardhacandreṇa ciccheda droṇasya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Hearing those words of theirs, Kṣatradharman, taking his stand, cut off with a crescent-headed arrow Droṇa's bow together with the shaft set upon it.

sanskrit: sa saṃrabdhataro bhūtvā droṇaḥ kṣatriyamardanaḥ anyat kārmukam ādāya bhāsvaraṃ vegavattaram
english: Grown the more furious thereat, Droṇa, the crusher of warriors, took up another bow, shining and of swifter force.

sanskrit: tatrādhāya śaraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ bhāraghnaṃ vimalaṃ dṛḍham ākarṇapūrṇam ācāryo balavān abhyavāsṛjat
english: Fitting to it a keen arrow, burden-destroying, bright and firm, the mighty preceptor drew it to the ear and let it fly.

sanskrit: sa hatvā kṣatradharmāṇaṃ jagāma dharaṇītalam sa bhinnahṛdayo vāhād apatan medinītale
english: That arrow, having slain Kṣatradharman, passed on into the surface of the earth; and he, his heart cleft, fell from his car upon the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ sainyāny akampanta dhṛṣṭadyumnasute hate atha droṇaṃ samārohac cekitāno mahārathaḥ
english: Then, when the son of Dhṛṣṭadyumna was slain, the armies trembled; and the great car-warrior Cekitāna closed upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa droṇaṃ daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyat stanāntare caturbhiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya caturbhiś caturo hayān
english: He pierced Droṇa with ten arrows between the breasts, his charioteer with four, and his four horses with four.

sanskrit: tasyācāryaḥ ṣoḍaśabhir avidhyad dakṣiṇaṃ bhujam dhvajaṃ ṣoḍaśabhir bāṇair yantāraṃ cāsya saptabhiḥ
english: The preceptor pierced his right arm with sixteen arrows, his standard with sixteen, and his driver with seven.

sanskrit: tasya sūte hate te 'śvā ratham ādāya vidrutāḥ samare śarasaṃvītā bhāradvājena māriṣa
english: When his charioteer was slain, those horses, enwrapped in the arrows of the son of Bharadvāja, bolted in the battle, dragging the car away, O noble one.

sanskrit: cekitānarathaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidrutaṃ hatasārathim pāñcālān pāṇḍavāṃś caiva mahad bhayam athāviśat
english: Seeing Cekitāna's car bolting with its charioteer slain, a great fear came over the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas alike.

sanskrit: tān sametān raṇe śūrāṃś cedipāñcālasṛñjayān samantād drāvayan droṇo bahv aśobhata māriṣa
english: Routing on every side those gathered heroes in the battle—the Cedis, the Pāñcālas, and the Sṛñjayas—Droṇa shone forth in great splendour, O noble one.

sanskrit: ākarṇapalitaḥ śyāmo vayasāśītikāt paraḥ raṇe paryacarad droṇo vṛddhaḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣavat
english: Grey to the ears and dark of hue, past eighty years of age, the aged Droṇa ranged through the battle like a youth of sixteen.

sanskrit: atha droṇaṃ mahārāja vicarantam abhītavat vajrahastam amanyanta śatravaḥ śatrusūdanam
english: And his foes, O great king, deemed Droṇa, the slayer of foes, ranging fearlessly, to be Indra himself with the thunderbolt in his hand.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahārāja drupado buddhimān nṛpa lubdho 'yaṃ kṣatriyān hanti vyāghraḥ kṣudramṛgān iva
english: Then, O great king, the wise Drupada spoke, O monarch: "This greedy man slays the warriors as a tiger slays small game."

sanskrit: kṛcchrān duryodhano lokān pāpaḥ prāpsyati durmatiḥ yasya lobhād vinihatāḥ samare kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: "The wicked, evil-minded Duryodhana shall come to grievous realms—he through whose greed the bulls among the warriors are slain in battle."

sanskrit: śataśaḥ śerate bhūmau nikṛttā govṛṣā iva rudhireṇa parītāṅgāḥ śvasṛgālādanīkṛtāḥ
english: "By the hundred they lie upon the earth, cut down like bulls, their limbs bathed in blood, made food for dogs and jackals."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja drupado 'kṣauhiṇīpatiḥ puraskṛtya raṇe pārthān droṇam abhyadravad drutam
english: Having spoken thus, O great king, Drupada, lord of an army, placing the sons of Pṛthā at the front, swiftly rushed upon Droṇa in battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vyūheṣv āloḍyamāneṣu pāṇḍavānāṃ tatas tataḥ sudūram anvayuḥ pārthāḥ pāñcālāḥ saha somakaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As the battle-arrays of the Pāṇḍavas were thrown into turmoil here and there, the sons of Pṛthā, the Pāñcālas, and the Somakas pursued the foe far afield.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā raudre saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe prakṣaye jagatas tīvre yugānta iva bhārata
english: While that fierce battle, hair-raising, raged on in the dire destruction of the world, as at the ending of an age, O descendant of Bharata—

sanskrit: droṇe yudhi parākrānte nardamāne muhur muhuḥ pāñcāleṣu ca kṣīṇeṣu vadhyamāneṣu pāṇḍuṣu
english: —while Droṇa pressed valiantly in the fight, roaring again and again, and the Pāñcālas dwindled and the Pāṇḍavas were being slain—

sanskrit: nāpaśyac charaṇaṃ kiṃ cid dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ cintayām āsa rājendra katham etad bhaviṣyati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of righteousness, saw no refuge anywhere, and pondered, O lord of kings: "How shall this end?"

sanskrit: tatrāvekṣya diśaḥ sarvāḥ savyasācididṛkṣayā yudhiṣṭhiro dadarśātha naiva pārthaṃ na mādhavam
english: Looking then in every direction with a longing to behold Savyasācin, Yudhiṣṭhira saw neither the son of Pṛthā nor the descendant of Madhu.

sanskrit: so 'paśyan naraśārdūlaṃ vānararṣabhalakṣaṇam gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣam aśṛṇvan vyathitendriyaḥ
english: Not seeing that tiger among men marked by the standard of the bull among monkeys, and not hearing the twang of the Gāṇḍīva, his senses were stricken with distress.

sanskrit: apaśyan sātyakiṃ cāpi vṛṣṇīnāṃ pravaraṃ ratham cintayābhiparītāṅgo dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nādhyagacchat tadā śāntiṃ tāv apaśyan nararṣabhau
english: Nor seeing Sātyaki either, that foremost car-warrior of the Vṛṣṇis, the king of righteousness Yudhiṣṭhira, his whole frame overcome with anxiety, found then no peace, beholding not those two bulls among men.

sanskrit: lokopakrośabhīrutvād dharmarājo mahāyaśāḥ acintayan mahābāhuḥ śaineyasya rathaṃ prati
english: From fear of the world's reproach, the greatly renowned king of righteousness, of mighty arms, fell to musing concerning the chariot of the grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: padavīṃ preṣitaś caiva phalgunasya mayā raṇe śaineyaḥ sātyakiḥ satyo mitrāṇām abhayaṃkaraḥ
english: "By me has the grandson of Śini, the true Sātyaki, giver of fearlessness to his friends, been sent upon the track of Phalguna in the battle."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ hy ekam evāsīd dvidhā jātaṃ mamādya vai sātyakiś ca hi me jñeyaḥ pāṇḍavaś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "What was once a single care has now become twofold for me this day: for I must look both to Sātyaki and to the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya."

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ preṣayitvā tu pāṇḍavasya padānugam sātvatasyāpi kaṃ yuddhe preṣayiṣye padānugam
english: "Having sent Sātyaki to follow upon the track of the Pāṇḍava, whom now shall I send in the battle to follow upon the track of the Sātvata as well?"

sanskrit: kariṣyāmi prayatnena bhrātur anveṣaṇaṃ yadi yuyudhānam ananviṣya loko māṃ garhayiṣyati
english: "If with all effort I make search for my brother, yet seek not after Yuyudhāna, the world will censure me."

sanskrit: bhrātur anveṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ parityajati vārṣṇeyaṃ sātyakiṃ satyavikramam
english: "'In searching for his brother, Yudhiṣṭhira the king of righteousness has forsaken the Vṛṣṇi Sātyaki of true valour'—so will they say."

sanskrit: lokāpavādabhīrutvāt so 'haṃ pārthaṃ vṛkodaram padavīṃ preṣayiṣyāmi mādhavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "From fear of the world's blame, I shall therefore send the son of Pṛthā, Vṛkodara, upon the track of the high-souled descendant of Madhu."

sanskrit: yathaiva ca mama prītir arjune śatrusūdane tathaiva vṛṣṇivīre 'pi sātvate yuddhadurmade
english: "For even as is my love for Arjuna, the slayer of foes, so too is it for that Vṛṣṇi hero, the Sātvata, fierce and unrelenting in battle."

sanskrit: atibhāre niyuktaś ca mayā śaineyanandanaḥ sa tu mitroparodhena gauravāc ca mahābalaḥ praviṣṭo bhāratīṃ senāṃ makaraḥ sāgaraṃ yathā
english: "To an overwhelming burden have I appointed the joy of Śini's line; and he, mighty in strength, out of regard for his friends and out of reverence, has entered the Bhārata host as a sea-monster plunges into the ocean."

sanskrit: asau hi śrūyate śabdaḥ śūrāṇām anivartinām mithaḥ saṃyudhyamānānāṃ vṛṣṇivīreṇa dhīmatā
english: "For yonder is heard the clamour of warriors who turn not back, locked in mutual combat with the wise hero of the Vṛṣṇis."
